arxiv-2204-10309.title: On a conjecture of Talagrand on selector processes and a consequence on positive empirical processes
arxiv-2204-10309.creator: Jinyoung Park and Huy Tuan Pham
arxiv-2204-10309.description: Abstract . For appropriate Gaussian processes, as a corollary of the majorizing measure theorem, Michel Talagrand (1987) proved that the event that the supremum is significantly larger than its expectation can be covered by a set of half-spaces whose sum of measures is small.

arxiv-2207-09836.title: Inverse Design of Whispering-gallery Nanolasers with Tailored Beam Shape and Polarization
arxiv-2207-09836.creator: Iago Diez, Andrey Krysa, Isaac J. Luxmoore
arxiv-2207-09836.description: Abstract Control over the shape and polarization of the beam emitted by a laser source is important in applications such as optical communications, optical manipulation and high-resolution optical imaging. In this paper, we present the inverse design of monolithic whispering-gallery nanolasers which emit along their axial direction with a tailored laser beam shape and polarization.

arxiv-2301-02751.creator: Dragomir Ž. ¯ Doković
arxiv-2301-02751.description: Abstract . The smallest integer v > 0 v>0 for which no skew-Hadamard matrix of order 4 ​ v 4v is known is v = 69 v=69 . We show how to construct several such matrices. We also construct the first examples of a skew Hadamard matrix of order 292 and symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 372.

arxiv-2306-00732.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David P. Woodruff, Taisuke Yasuda. In large scale machine learning, random sampling is a popular way to approximate datasets by a small representative subset of examples. In particular, sensitivity sampling is an intensely studied technique which provides provable guarantees on the quality of approximation, while reducing the number of examples to the product of the VC dimension d d and the total sensitivity 𝔖 \mathfrak{S} in remarkably general settings.

arxiv-2311-02774.title: A stronger connection between the asymptotic rank conjecture and the set cover conjecture
arxiv-2311-02774.creator: Kevin Pratt
arxiv-2311-02774.description: Abstract We give a short proof that Strassen’s asymptotic rank conjecture implies that for every ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 there exists a ( 3 / 2 2 / 3 + ε ) n (3/2^{2/3}+\varepsilon)^{n} -time algorithm for set cover on a universe of size n n with sets of bounded size.

arxiv-2401-08606.title: Forking paths in financial economics
arxiv-2401-08606.creator: Guillaume Coqueret
arxiv-2401-08606.description: Abstract We argue that spanning large numbers of degrees of freedom in empirical analysis allows better characterizations of effects and thus improves the trustworthiness of conclusions. Our ideas are illustrated in three studies: equity premium prediction, asset pricing anomalies and risk premia estimation.

arxiv-2412-01609.title: Optimizing LoRa for Edge Computing with TinyML Pipeline for Channel Hopping
arxiv-2412-01609.creator: Marla Grunewald, Mounir Bensalem and Admela Jukan
arxiv-2412-01609.description: Abstract We propose to integrate long-distance LongRange (LoRa) communication solution for sending the data from IoT to the edge computing system, by taking advantage of its unlicensed nature and the potential for open source implementations that are common in edge computing.

britannica-1911-cornelius-carl-august-pe.description: Article 'Cornelius, Carl August Peter' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 7), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. painter, was born at Mainz on the 24th of December 1824. In his childhood his bent was towards languages, but his musical gifts were carefully cultivated and he learned to sing and to play the violin. Cornelius the elder, anxious for his son to become an actor, himself taught the boy the elements of the art.

pmc-10739761.title: High-throughput phenotyping of nutritional quality components in sweet potato roots by near-infrared spectroscopy and chemometrics methods
pmc-10739761.creator: Chaochen Tang, Bingzhi Jiang, Irsa Ejaz, Asif Ameen, Rong Zhang, Xueying Mo, Zhangying Wang
pmc-10739761.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Highlights•Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) was used to quality evaluation of sweet potato.•Eight optimized NIRS models were developed for rapid content determination.•NIRS applicable for large-scale screening of sweet potato germplasm. Introduction

Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam) is a major root crop that plays an indispensable role in ensuring food security and improving diversified diets due to its high yield potential and health-promoting values (Alam, 2021, Wang et al., 2016).

pmc-11434920.title: Genetic Diversity, Virulence, and Antibiotic Resistance Determinants of Campylobacter jejuni Isolates in Romania
pmc-11434920.creator: Madalina Baltoiu, Gratiela Gradisteanu Pircalabioru, Daniela Cristea, Marilena Sorokin, Cristiana Cerasella Dragomirescu, Ileana Stoica
pmc-11434920.description: The emergence of antibiotic-resistant Campylobacter jejuni, a leading cause of gastroenteritis worldwide, presents a significant public health challenge requiring vigilant surveillance and disease control. This study aimed to characterize C. jejuni strains isolated in Romania from 2017 to 2020, focusing on genetic diversity, virulence, and antibiotic resistance determinants.

pmc-11494452.title: Pde3a and Pde3b regulation of murine pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell growth and metabolism
pmc-11494452.creator: Paulina N. Krause, Gabrielle McGeorge, Jennifer L. McPeek, Sidra Khalid, Leif D. Nelin, Yusen Liu, Bernadette Chen
pmc-11494452.description: A role for metabolically active adipose tissue in pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis is emerging. Alterations in cellular metabolism in metabolic syndrome are triggers of PH‐related vascular dysfunction. Metabolic reprogramming in proliferative pulmonary vascular cells causes a metabolic switch from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis.

pmc-12356975.title: Androgens drive SLC1A5-dependent metabolic reprogramming in polycystic ovary syndrome
pmc-12356975.creator: Yishu Wang, Jiaying Wu, Gaochen Zhang, Yan Shi, Yicong Meng, Pingping Lv, Weiwei Huang, Yunfei Su, Zhiyang Zhou, Bo Wang, Xiaojun Chen, Chengliang Zhou, Jiexue Pan, Li Jin, Xiaotao Wang, Yanting Wu, Jianzhong Sheng, Xinmei Liu, Yu Zhang, Guolian Ding, Chuanjin Yu, Hefeng Huang
pmc-12356975.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome is the primary cause of female infertility. Growing evidence suggests that dysregulation of amino acid metabolism plays a significant role in the onset and progression. However, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we conduct targeted metabolite profiling of human follicular fluid and granulosa cells.

pmc-12692688.title: Transcriptional Responses to Alkaline pH Across Fungi: Common and Differential Features, and Biotechnological Applications
pmc-12692688.creator: Joaquín Ariño, Makoto Kimura
pmc-12692688.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The transcriptional response to alkalinization in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Aspergillus nidulans and Candida albicans raised the interest of the scientific community many years ago for diverse reasons, and the underlying signaling pathways have been elucidated in these organisms in detail. Within the last few years, transcriptomic data for other fungal species have become available, although in most cases little is known about the molecular basis controlling their adaptive response.

pmc-13214319.title: Differential expression of microRNAs in the prefrontal cortex as indicators of sheep welfare
pmc-13214319.creator: Sarah Babington, Luoyang Ding, Alan J Tilbrook, Shane K Maloney, Dominique Blache
pmc-13214319.description: BackgroundIndicators that are used to assess animal welfare tend to be non-specific and provide limited information on how a situation is experienced by an animal. There is growing evidence that microRNAs could be useful biomarkers of brain function and experience in humans, however, there has been limited work evaluating their use for assessing experience, and thus the welfare of animals.

pmc-13552828.title: Making Patient-reported Outcome Measures Patient-friendly: Applying “Patient-reported Outcomes Tools: Engaging Users and Stakeholders” Guidelines to a Graphical “Report Card” for Cleft Outcomes
pmc-13552828.creator: Elaine Lin, Marina Sawires, Katie Brown, Angel Scialdone, Tara Pillai, Victoria Yi, Meredith Cox, Kamlesh Patel, Christopher Runyan, Alexander C. Allori
pmc-13552828.description: Background:Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), such as the CLEFT-Q, provide valuable insights into the psychosocial and functional well-being of patients with cleft lip and/or palate. Ideally, PROM data should not only inform clinicians and researchers but should also be shared back with patients and families; however, no guidelines exist for formatting CLEFT-Q data for patient review.

pmc-13607193.title: OsbZIP60 Positively Regulates Salt-Stress Tolerance in Rice
pmc-13607193.creator: Liqun Tang, Honghuan Fan, Junmin Wang, Kaizhen Zhong, Kunquan Liu, Mingli Han, Jian Song
pmc-13607193.description: Soil salinity is a major abiotic stress limiting rice growth and grain productivity worldwide. Basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factors serve as central regulators of plant environmental stress responses, yet the biological function and molecular regulatory mechanism of rice OsbZIP60 (LOC_Os07g44950) underlying salinity tolerance remain largely uncharacterized.
